reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold and routes the inline midpoint copies and the existing getScheduledAmount through one helper, but introduces getPlannedAmount next to the existing exported getScheduledAmount rather than evolving that one helper.

duplication.why: All five midpoint copies are replaced by calls to the shared function; getScheduledAmount delegates instead of repeating.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount; the API field is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps; some stale comments ('end furthest from zero') and release notes from earlier steps contradict the final rule.

maintainability.why: Two public helpers for one decision and an optional op parameter mean callers that forget it (most desktop-client callers) silently skip the approximate rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No site keeps its own amount resolution; all call getPlannedAmount or getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount delegates to getPlannedAmount; no reshaped copy remains.

abstraction_drift.where: Optional op added to shared getScheduledAmount and an isapprox branch in getPlannedAmount; only Balance.tsx passes op, while SchedulesTable, SchedulesListItem, MobileSchedulesPage and useScheduleEdit still call without it; forecast-schedules adds an _amountOp ?? condition op fallback.
